title: Biofabrication of Immunocompetent Tumor-on-Chip Models for Anticancer Therapy Assessment
author: Nurmik, Ladaigue, et al.

steps.title: Prepare spheroid media
steps.instruction: Prepare Spheroid Media (Stock) and Spheroid Media (Final) according to the protocol, store the stock for up to 1 month, use the final media within one week, and pre‑warm all media at 37 °C for 20 min before use.

steps.title: Seed primary tumor cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tumor‑cell‑containing fraction for 10 min at 400–500 g, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 12 mL Spheroid Media (Final) and transfer to a T75 Ultra‑Low‑Attachment Flask (Corning #3814). For low cell counts (<5 × 10⁵), resuspend in 3 mL Spheroid Media (Final) and add to one well of a 6‑well Ultra‑Low‑Attachment plate (Corning #3471).

steps.title: Incubate and feed spheroids
steps.instruction: Place the flask (or plate) in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator and feed with Spheroid Media (Final) every two days. Cultures may be maintained under normoxic (20 % O₂) or hypoxic (1.5 % O₂) conditions; optional lower O₂ (1–5 %) can improve growth but is not required.

steps.title: Passage tumor spheroids
steps.instruction: When spheroid diameter reaches ~300–400 µm, transfer the suspension to a 50 mL tube, centrifuge at 350 g for 5 min, discard supernatant, add 3–5 mL PBS (Gibco #10010023) and centrifuge again at 350 g for 5 min. Remove supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL TrypLE Express Enzyme (Gibco #12605010), pipette up/down 20 times with a P1000, incubate at 37 °C for 3 min, repeat the pipetting step, add 3 mL Spheroid Media (Final) to inactivate TrypLE, centrifuge at 350 g for 5 min, discard supernatant and resuspend cells in Spheroid Media (Final) or required assay media. For long‑term storage, resuspend the pellet in 0.5–1 mL Synth‑a‑Freeze Cryopreservation Medium (Gibco #A1254201) and freeze at –80 °C briefly before transfer to liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Prepare CD8+ TIL media
steps.instruction: Prepare Medium A and pre‑warm at 37 °C for 20 min before use.

steps.title: Isolate and seed CD8+ TILs
steps.instruction: Count CD8+ cells and viability, centrifuge the CD8+ fraction for 10 min at 400–500 g, discard supernatant, resuspend cells in Medium A supplemented with 30 ng/mL recombinant IL‑2 (Gibco #PHC0021) to obtain ~5 000 cells per 100 µL. Seed 200 µL (≈10 000 cells) per well into a V‑bottom 96‑well plate (Greiner #651261) and incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Culture under 20 % O₂; replace IL‑2‑containing media weekly. For expansion, collect cells, centrifuge 10 min at 400–500 g, and re‑plate at 5 000 cells per 100 µL. For long‑term storage, freeze cells in Medium A with IL‑2 and 10 % DMSO, store at –80 °C then transfer to liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Prepare fibroblast media
steps.instruction: Prepare fibroblast media, store up to one month, and pre‑warm at 37 °C for 20 min before use.

steps.title: Isolate and plate CAFs
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the non‑tumor cell fraction for 10 min at 400–500 g, discard supernatant, resuspend cells in fibroblast media and plate 200 000–500 000 cells per petri dish (Greiner #353003). Transfer dishes to a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator and change fibroblast media every two days. Optional lower O₂ (1–5 %) may improve growth.

steps.title: Passage cancer‑associated fibroblasts
steps.instruction: When CAFs reach ~80 % confluence, remove supernatant, wash with 10 mL PBS, discard PBS, add 1 mL TrypLE Express Enzyme, incubate at 37 °C for 5 min and verify detachment (tap dish if needed). Add 9 mL fibroblast media to inactivate TrypLE (if cells remain attached, vigorously wash with neutralizing media). Transfer suspension to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge 3–5 min at 350 g, discard supernatant, resuspend in desired volume, count cells and viability. For continuous culture, seed 250 000 cells per 10‑cm dish. For freezing, suspend cells in fibroblast medium with 10 % DMSO, store at –80 °C then transfer to liquid nitrogen.

description: Here, we introduce a protocol designed for the development of patient-derived autologous tumor-on-chips (ToCs), utilizing a readily accessible commercial microfluidic device (AIM-Biotech, #DAX-1), with the main objective of assessing therapy efficacy. While tailored for primary patient tissue utilization, the described ToC model can be easily adapted to any cell type (e.g., human or murine, primary or immortalized, transfected or genetically edited). The protocol outlined below enables the creation of a multipopulational, immunocompetent, 3D ToC model using relatively low cell counts (20,000 – 40,000 cells in total), suitable for small surgical samples (range size of 1-2 cm3). Additionally, this protocol is well-suited for the quick reconstitution of the patient’s cell co-cultures immediately after surgery, preserving the highest possible degree of similarity to in vivo cell identities and properties. This protocol outlines two tumor-on-chip (ToC) approaches: post-dissociation and post-amplification ToCs. Post-dissociation ToCs are assembled immediately after tumor resection and typically involve cell types that can be isolated at relatively high yields, such as epithelial tumor cells and CD8+ T cells. For this approach, the isolated cells can be directly utilized following primary tumor dissociation. Users can proceed straight to the “Encapsulation of primary cells in collagen-based tumor-on-chips (ToCs)” section of the protocol if freshly isolated cells are used. Post-amplification ToCs are recommended for cell types that are isolated in lower numbers from the tumor sample, such as cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) or cells which are difficult to isolate with a high degree of purity. In these cases, cultivation or amplification of the cells is necessary before their incorporation into the ToC.
